conditions.model: host register model of the startup sequencer, domain 4 OFF for the cold enable

narrative: Host models execute no NPU arithmetic, so they give startup times but no job time. Table: modelled boot to READY with a cold enable and domain 4 OFF: 4,628 us at 492 MHz and 4,628 us at 852 MHz. Modelled boot to READY for a rate change of a running PLL from the other profile: 4,615 us (from 852 MHz to 492 MHz) and 4,615 us (from 492 MHz to 852 MHz). PLL writes in a rate change: 5 at either rate. The 852 MHz profile was checked in the host model and on the linked instructions of the finite image built with --rate-852; the user approved NPU clock changes on 2026-10-25, 852 MHz first at the inherited 800 mV (bringup handoff, commit 3c17aeca); NPU voltage changes were not approved, and nothing writes DCDC2. The three-start runbook (docs/board-runbooks/npu-starts.md) runs the 492 to 852 MHz rate change last in a lifetime. The profile is rank 6 of the vendor action plan.

hypothesis: A job at 852 MHz computes in 492/852 = 0.58 of its 492 MHz time with byte-identical outputs
prediction: Predicted job time on the board, publication to completion observation: one poll period, under 1 ms, at both 492 MHz and 852 MHz. The finite client logs each job's publication and completion observation in counter microseconds, and the host reports them. The service worker polls for completion once per 1 ms tick in the polled profile, so a job shorter than a tick reads as the time to the next poll at either rate. The NPU's compute time is predicted to scale by 492/852 = 0.58, less where memory bounds the work. The interrupt profile resolves it: it times each job from publication to interrupt 97 and counts the NPU's active cycles (docs/designs/npu-irq-completion.md). The outputs are predicted to be byte-identical at both rates.
conclusion: Not yet run as a comparison of the two rates in one lifetime. Board runs of the OS NPU service at 852 MHz and 800 mV are recorded in docs/evidence/npu.jsonl; none times the same graph at 492 MHz.
narrative: Prediction for a run that has not happened: the host models give startup times only, so the job-time comparison between 492 MHz and 852 MHz waits for a board run of the finite numerical image at both rates (three-start runbook, docs/board-runbooks/npu-starts.md).
